rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Bavarian procedures are outside what this product covers. We cover federal law, Hessen state procedures and the Indian consular track. The Elterngeld (parental allowance) rules below are federal law, so they also apply in Bavaria. How to apply in Bavaria, and which office handles it, must come from the office responsible for Elterngeld in Bavaria.

Who can claim. A parent has a claim if they live in Germany, live in one household with the child, care for and raise the child themselves, and do no work or no full-time work ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt").

Self-employed income counts. Elterngeld is 67 percent of income from work before the birth. That income includes positive income from a trade or business and from self-employed work ("Gewerbebetrieb und selbständiger Arbeit") that is taxable in Germany, minus deductions for taxes and social contributions. For full months with no income from work, the maximum is 1,800 euros a month. The minimum is 300 euros.

Provisional decisions. The amount is decided provisionally, based on the figures the parent has credibly stated, in three cases:
- when the tax assessment notice for the last completed assessment period before the birth ("Steuerbescheid für den letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum") is not yet available;
- when income before the birth cannot be determined;
- when the parent expects to have income from work during the benefit period.

The final decision waits until the required figures are proven.

After the benefit period. If the application stated expected income from work, the actual income for that period must be proven once the benefit period ends. If the application stated no expected income, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation ("unter dem Vorbehalt des Widerrufs") in case income does arise.

What these excerpts do not cover. They do not say which period of self-employed income is used for the calculation, or exactly how that income is worked out. Ask the office responsible for Elterngeld in Bavaria. That office decides whether you qualify and how much you receive. Applications are submitted there.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
We cannot fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application for you. The form asks you to make choices and state figures about your own family, and those are decisions about your individual case. What we can do is tell you what the law says the application must contain.

What the law requires:
- The application must be made in writing: "Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen" (BEEG §7(1)).
- The application must state which months of the child's life you are claiming, and which of the three payment types the law names you want for each month (BEEG §7(1)).
- It must be signed by the person applying. The other entitled parent must also sign, to confirm they have seen it. This does not apply to a parent with sole custody or in the case of §4c (BEEG §7(3)).
- Payment is made backwards only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid (BEEG §7(1)).
- Your choices in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period (BEEG §7(2)).
- If you give expected earnings in the application, you must prove your actual earnings for that time after the payment period ends (BEEG §8(1)).

Documents to attach, according to the federal family portal:
- your child's birth certificate
- proof of your previous income, for example payslips for the last 12 months
- further documents, depending on your situation

Your employer is obliged to issue the documents you need.

Who decides and where to go: each state names the office responsible for Elterngeld. The responsible office is the one for the district where your child lives when you first apply (BEEG §12(1)). That office receives your application and decides on it. The excerpts we have do not name the specific office in Hessen. Contact the Elterngeld office for your district in Hessen for help with the form and for binding information about your own case.
